_comment: One RSS feed per entry. Each entry carries a `regions` array of
ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 codes plus 'GLOBAL' for non-region-specific.
Set `enabled: false` to skip a source without removing it.
Malformed XML or 404s log a warning and are skipped — never crash.
_notes_on_substitutions: FT — Companies: regions UK+EU+GLOBAL (London-headquartered, EU+UK governance focus)
Original ask 'NYT Business RSS': substituted for `nyt-business` -> NYT Business top-level feed which works.
Original ask 'Handelsblatt English': RSS no longer publishes English; substituted with `politico-eu-business` (Europe-focused, English-language, RSS public).
Original ask 'Nikkei Asia Business': RSS not public; substituted with `scmp-business` (South China Morning Post — Asia-business focus, RSS public).
Original ask 'Business Day South Africa': RSS not public; substituted with `aljazeera-business` (pan-Africa+global coverage, RSS public). Best fit for Africa region tag in the curated set.
_africa_expansion_2026_05_27: Task 3 (2026-05-27) — Free, executive-grade Africa-focused sources added on user request:
User mandate: 'Do what's free but effective, include Africa, East Africa, Nairobi as most users will be here.'
bbc-africa  — BBC News — Africa, free RSS, EN, pan-Africa coverage.
quartz-africa — Quartz Africa, free RSS, EN, business-focused pan-Africa.
businessdaily-africa — Business Daily Africa (Nairobi), free RSS, EN, KE business.
the-east-african — The East African (Nairobi-based), free RSS, EN, KE/UG/TZ/RW coverage.
nation-africa — Nation Africa (NMG/Daily Nation), free RSS, EN, KE general+business.
standard-kenya — The Standard (Kenya), free RSS, EN, KE general+business.
Dead-feed policy: the aggregator already silently skips malformed/404 feeds; if any of these break in production, set enabled:false instead of removing.
_removed_2026_05_26_redeploy_cleanup: Four sources removed during the 2026-05-26 redeploy-cleanup chunk after HEAD probes confirmed the underlying RSS endpoints are dead. Documented here so future maintainers know what was tried (and why each was pulled rather than `enabled: false`-d).
reuters-biz — was https://feeds.reuters.com/reuters/businessNews — DNS resolution fails (`feeds.reuters.com` retired); Reuters discontinued public RSS.
hbr — was https://hbr.org/feed — HTTP 404 (Harvard Business Review retired the feed URL).
frc-uk — was https://www.frc.org.uk/news-and-events/rss — HTTP 404 (Financial Reporting Council UK changed CMS; old RSS path gone).
iod — was https://www.iod.com/news/rss — HTTP 403 (Institute of Directors blocks unauth probes + does not serve RSS at that path).
Replacement sources are NOT auto-substituted here — that's a follow-up decision the operator opted to defer.
